Rish local patch to gpui-pre-wgpu 0.3.6

Upstream and license
The 14 upstream files are copied from the registry package identified in
UPSTREAM.toml, including its normalized Cargo.toml, Cargo.toml.orig and full
Apache-2.0 license. The official crate archive was verified against the
checksum in the mobile workspace lockfile and compared byte for byte with
the source before modification. The archive contains no NOTICE or Cargo VCS
metadata. Its Cargo.lock is preserved as upstream package content; the
application resolves dependencies through apps/gpui/mobile/Cargo.lock.

Change
Only src/wgpu_context.rs and src/wgpu_renderer.rs are modified from the upstream
snapshot. The local
src/wgpu_backend_policy.rs module centralizes and tests backend policy.
In the native instance constructor,
Android removes InstanceFlags::DEBUG from the default flags. VALIDATION,
VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL and all other default flags are unchanged. Other
platforms keep the original default flags. The mobile workspace selects this
copy with its crates.io path patch; no global Cargo cache is modified.

Both browser WebGL and native OpenGL ES use downlevel_webgl2_defaults limits
and the existing texture-based instance transport. Native(Gl) no longer uses
storage-buffer shaders merely because the target is not wasm. GL does not
request dual-source blending, which this transport does not use, and prefers
RGBA atlas textures when supported, as the browser GL path already did.
Vulkan, Metal, DX12 and browser WebGPU keep their existing downlevel limits
and storage transport. No shader algorithms or adapter priority are changed.

Reason
wgpu-hal 29.0.4 uses DEBUG to request Naga SPIR-V debug records whose OpSource
language is WGSL (10). An Android API 34 arm64 emulator using the existing
SwiftShader backend reported "Invalid source language operand: 10" while
vkCreateGraphicsPipelines blocked the initial GPUI window creation. The
Android main thread then waited for the native event loop to acknowledge
Pause. This patch removes that diagnostic metadata without disabling GPU
validation, changing rendering shaders, or bypassing lifecycle acknowledgments.

Validation boundary
The package checksum, copied files, license, Android-only flag difference and
source formatting have been checked. Emulator acceptance for the added GLES
path is recorded below. This compatibility patch does not establish that the
earlier Vulkan ANR or the API 33 SwiftShader Vulkan corruption is fixed.

Native GLES compatibility
On the Android API 33 GLES emulator, the GL adapter reports no compute support
(max_compute_workgroups_per_dimension = 0). The old native path requested
downlevel_defaults (65535), so device creation failed before the first frame.
The same adapter cannot use the storage-buffer instance path. Limits and
transport must be selected together by actual backend, not compilation target.

The backend-policy unit tests cover an adapter without compute/storage buffers,
adapter resolution/alignment, unchanged non-GL policy, and dual-source feature
selection. Run them against the same wgpu-types 29.0.4 version as the mobile
lockfile; they do not require a GPU. Actual GLES rendering and input/lifecycle
checks still require an APK running on a device or emulator. This fallback does
not establish that artifacts observed with the Vulkan renderer are fixed.

Explicit backend selection
The native instance now honors wgpu's standard WGPU_BACKEND override, using
Backends::with_env before creating any surface. With no override it still
enables Vulkan and GL and retains the existing adapter priority. An explicit
WGPU_BACKEND=gl creates only the GL surface. This is needed on Android because
creating a Vulkan surface can acquire the native window before GL configures
its EGL surface; filtering Vulkan adapters afterward does not release that
connection. The override is opt-in and process-scoped, not a device-wide
emulator configuration or an automatic fallback after a renderer failure.

The backend policy test exercises the actual wgpu environment parser in child
processes (unset, gl, vulkan), without mutating the parallel test runner's
environment. Pixel and lifecycle acceptance remains a device/emulator check.

Surface replacement on resume
Android supplies a preferred Mailbox presentation mode both at startup and
after recreating its native window. Initial renderer setup already checked
surface capabilities and chose Fifo on a Fifo-only GLES surface, but
replace_surface copied Mailbox unconditionally. Resume then failed surface
configuration and attempted to acquire a texture from an unconfigured surface.

Initial setup and replacement now share a supported-present-mode policy.
Replacement queries the new surface with the existing context's adapter and
uses the preferred mode only if supported; otherwise it selects Fifo. Without
a new preference, the previous mode is retained only when the new surface
supports it. Supported Mailbox configurations on other backends are preserved.
Pure policy tests cover the Fifo-only startup/resume case and a change in
surface capabilities. Actual background/resume and pixel verification must
still be run on the resulting APK; this policy test is not lifecycle evidence.

Native surface ownership
unconfigure_surface now drops the actual wgpu Surface, releasing its native
EGL/Vulkan connection, while keeping the device, queue, atlas and pipelines.
An unavailable surface is represented separately from a retained renderer.
Draw and resize skip detached surfaces; transparency changes retain their
configuration without reconnecting a destroyed window. Replacement drops any
previous surface before creating the next, and publishes readiness only after
Surface::configure's device error scopes confirm success. Failed attempts stay
detached for the Android event loop's bounded retry. The Android caller releases
the surface before its NativeWindow reference and before the destruction ACK.

This ownership fix is separate from backend selection or shader transport.
The historical GLES acceptance below predates it. The rebuilt APK subsequently
passed four same-Activity stop/resume cycles, readiness and panel/title pixel
checks. It does not establish a fix for SwiftShader Vulkan itself.

2026-11-06 first GLES emulator evidence (historical)
The new ModelPickerRendererTest injects a real tap and checks that an empty
model panel is opaque in three captured frames, including after an Activity
CREATED -> RESUMED transition. On Pixel XL API 33 / arm64 with host GLES and
process-local WGPU_BACKEND=gl it passes after this patch; the resumed screenshot
was also inspected. Before the present-mode fix it failed after resume with
Mailbox unsupported on a Fifo-only surface. Before the GL path fixes, creation
failed on compute limits and then on the native-window connection.

The same popup test fails on the emulator's SwiftShader Vulkan path. This
remains a separate rendering defect. See the newer compatibility handling below;
no physical-device compatibility claim is made.

Known Android SwiftShader compatibility
Before creating any surface, default Android startup checks for an exclusively
known Vulkan adapter set: SwiftShader Device (LLVM 10.0.0), VirtualGpu, vendor
0x1ae0, device 0xc0de. Only if a GL adapter meets renderer limits, supports the
instance texture format and successfully creates a device is the old probe
instance dropped and a GL-only instance created. Empty, mixed, physical or
unknown Vulkan sets retain the existing backend mask; explicit WGPU_BACKEND
and ZED_DEVICE_ID overrides are never rewritten. Unusable GL also retains the
original mask. Adapter ranking, shader math and dependency pins are unchanged.

The original storage transport and a temporary Vulkan texture-transport A/B
both showed corruption; the diagnostic override was removed. On the final APK,
default host-GPU emulator startup selects GL and passes four detach/reattach
cycles with panel, title glyph and readiness assertions. Explicit Vulkan still
fails the pixel test. This is a narrow compatibility workaround, not a claimed
Vulkan driver fix. Full evidence is in docs/p0-android-2026-11-06.md.
